doc.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003

title: His father and the family band
summary: His father taught neighborhood kids, was a painter, carpenter and teacher, and Slide as youngest was handed the trombone.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: We were practicing and rehearsing every day. And all the people from the neighborhood were coming around. And the kids would come, and some of them would come in and learn about being musicians. My father was teaching everybody. He was a fantastic man.
Oh. And did he have work besides music too? During the day?

He did. My father could do everything. He was a great painter. He painted beautiful pictures. He was a carpenter. He was a school teacher. He did everything. That’s when you had that big family, he was actually very idealistic. Most people wouldn’t try to raise a family man, he had about ten kids you know. Most people wouldn’t try that. He didn’t think that was anything. He really felt as though he could handle that with no problem, because he could do so many things. And he did. He took care of us from the time that we were — until we were ready to leave home with no problem.
That’s wonderful. Do you have photos from back then?

I was just looking at my father and mother’s photos before I came here today, and a picture of our family band, one when I was very young and I wasn’t playing, I was dancing and singing in the band, and then one when I was older playing trombone.
That’s so interesting. Did you have people for a rhythm section, the whole—
Oh yeah. We had the rhythm section and everything right there in the family.
That’s neat. I sometimes wonder in those kind of situations your parents are thinking well let’s see, we need a saxophone player so—
I think that’s the way it was. They finally needed a trombone. I was the last one born into the family.
